precepts.point: Nevertheless the Lord thy God would not hearken unto Balaam, but turned the curse into a blessing, because the Lord thy God loveth thee; therefore Israel was never to seek their peace nor their prosperity.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

precepts.why:
The reason Ammon and Moab are shut out for ever: they met not Israel with bread and with water in the way when they came forth out of Egypt, “and because they hired against thee Balaam the son of Beor of Pethor of Mesopotamia, to curse thee.” The history is in Numbers.

“And Balak the son of Zippor saw all that Israel had done to the Amorites. And Moab was sore afraid of the people, because they were many”. Balak the son of Zippor, king of the Moabites, sent messengers unto Balaam the son of Beor to Pethor, saying, “Behold, there is a people come out from Egypt: behold, they cover the face of the earth, and they abide over against me: Come now therefore, I pray thee, curse me this people; for they are too mighty for me”. “And the elders of Moab and the elders of Midian departed with the rewards of divination in their hand”. That is the hiring of Balaam.

Nevertheless the Lord thy God would not hearken unto Balaam, but turned the curse into a blessing, because the Lord thy God loved thee; therefore Israel was never to seek their peace nor their prosperity all their days for ever.

precepts.text: The same Balaam the son of Beor that was sent for to curse Israel; he chased the reward and was slain.
precepts.point: With the princes of Midian, Balaam also the son of Beor, the soothsayer, did the children of Israel slay with the sword. This is the same Balaam from Numbers 22, the one whose ass saw the angel standing there to kill him when he could not see it himself. He was the one going after the lust of greed, and he ended up getting put to death.

note.label: Joshua 13: Much Land Yet to Be Possessed

precepts.why:
“Balaam also the son of Beor, the soothsayer, did the children of Israel slay with the sword among them that were slain by them.” This is the same Balaam from Numbers 22: “He sent messengers therefore unto Balaam the son of Beor to Pethor, which is by the river of the land of the children of his people, to call him”, sent for to curse Israel, the people come out from Egypt that “cover the face of the earth”.

He is the one whose ass saw the angel standing there to kill him when he could not see it himself. He was going after the lust of greed, chasing the reward, and it ended with him put to death with the sword alongside the princes of Midian, in the land that became the inheritance of the children of Reuben.

precepts.text: Balak hired Balaam to curse Israel, the history behind why the Ammonite and Moabite were shut out of the congregation.
precepts.point: When the people heard the law, they separated from Israel all the mixed multitude. The reading of the law produced immediate obedience, cutting off what the law said to cut off.

note.label: Nehemiah 13: Cleansing the People, the Sabbath, and the Strange Wives

precepts.why:
The law read that day said the Ammonite and the Moabite should not come into the congregation of God for ever because they “hired Balaam against them, that he should curse them”. This is that history. Balak “sent messengers therefore unto Balaam the son of Beor to Pethor”, saying, “Behold, there is a people come out from Egypt: behold, they cover the face of the earth, and they abide over against me: Come now therefore, I pray thee, curse me this people; for they are too mighty for me”.

Balak wanted Israel cursed so he could smite them and drive them out of the land, “for I wot that he whom thou blessest is blessed, and he whom thou cursest is cursed.” Hiring Balaam to curse Israel is why the Ammonite and Moabite were shut out of the congregation, and as Nehemiah says, “our God turned the curse into a blessing.”

precepts.text: The Most High told Balaam not to curse the people for they are blessed, refusing to let the king of Moab hire a curse upon Israel coming up out of Egypt.
precepts.point: The heavens are the Lord's, but the earth He has given to the children of men. The dead praise not the Lord, but we will bless the Lord from this time forth and forevermore.

note.label: Psalm 115: Not Unto Us, But Unto Thy Name Give Glory

precepts.why:
“He will bless them that fear the Lord, both small and great. The Lord shall increase you more and more, you and your children.” The scriptures say we are blessed, not cursed. “And God said unto Balaam, Thou shalt not go with them; thou shalt not curse the people: for they are blessed.”

The king of Moab tried to hire a curse upon Israel coming up out of Egypt, and the Most High refused to let it happen: they are blessed. This speaks of us as a nation, not of the brother or sister in the midst of sin claiming to be blessed and highly favored.

precepts.text: Balak king of Moab hired Balaam to curse Israel and pull them into idolatry; these nations have always been our enemies.
precepts.point: This is our salvation and redemption. Every nation has held Israel captive at one time, not just the friendly neighborhood white man: the Assyrians, Babylon, Persia and the Medes, Greece and Rome, the many captivities in the book of Judges, the Arabs and Ishmael in the trans-Saharan slave trade, and America. Whosoever leads into captivity shall go into captivity.

note.label: Jeremiah 49: Judgment on Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar, and Elam

precepts.why:
Balak king of Moab “sent messengers therefore unto Balaam the son of Beor to Pethor”, saying “Behold, there is a people come out from Egypt: behold, they cover the face of the earth, and they abide over against me: Come now therefore, I pray thee, curse me this people; for they are too mighty for me”. He hired Balaam to curse Israel and pull them into idolatry, for he said, “I wot that he whom thou blessest is blessed, and he whom thou cursest is cursed.”

That is who Moab and Ammon are to us: these nations have always been our enemies. So when the Most High says both Moab and Ammon go into captivity, it is because of what they did to Israel, and whosoever leads into captivity shall go into captivity. The reckoning on them comes first, and afterward their captivity is brought again. This is our salvation and redemption.
